JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIMS TRIBUNAL BIDAR AS  AGAINST THE APPELLANT BY ALLOWING THE APPEAL.

-2-  MFA No. 201138 of 2017  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

This appeal is preferred by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the Prl.Dist. & Sessions Judge and MACT, Bidar (for short 'Tribunal'), in MVC No.380/2016 dated 17.04.2017.
This appeal is founded on the premise of judgment being erroneous and illegal and seeks to set-aside the same.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 07.05.2016 at about 9:00 p.m. when petitioner was proceeding towards Zaheerabad on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/H-6366, near Shahapur gate,
opp.Hanuman Mandir, the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/S- 4534 ridden it in a most rash and negligent manner of riding due to which he lost control over the motorcycle and dashed against the petitioner and fled away from the spot and petitioner sustained multiple grievous injuries.

Due to the occurrence of accident, the claimant has expended huge amount towards medical expenses and incidental expenses and has sustained grievous injuries in the accident due to the rash and negligent driving by driver of the car.
Hence, he filed a claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is against the settled principles of law and justice.
The findings of the Tribunal on issue No.1 was erroneous and contrary to the evidence on record.
The claimant was discharged from Yashoda Hospital on 12.05.2016.
however, there is Ex.P7 which is the alleged further statement of the claimant claiming to have been identified the driver present in the police station.
The statement is stated to be recorded on 11.05.2016 but thereafter tampered to appear as 14.05.2016.
this piece of evidence contradicts the documentary evidence of the claimant which discloses that the was discharged from the Hospital on 12.05.2016.
When he was in Hospital how could he have seen the rider in the police station?

This is an indication of the facts that the rider was The National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Abdul Samad And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140939125/

sentences.text: subsequently, planted as the original rider was someone who obviously did not hold a driving licence.
Further it is submitted that MV report/Ex.P6 does not mention of any damage to the vehicle No.KA-38/H-6366 in the rear side.
If the vehicle of the claimant was hit from the rear, there is obviously ought to have been some damage to the rear side of the vehicle.
It also appears that the vehicle No.KA-38/S- 4534 was seized only on 13.05.2016.
Thus, it appears that the vehicle was also subsequently involved.
On all these grounds sought for allow this appeal.
5. Today, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant submitted memo along with certified copy of the records and submitted that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record.
The injured only after discharged on 14.05.2016 the police have recorded the further statement.
The police have not recorded the statement on 12.05.2016 as submitted by the appellant counsel.
The Investigating Officer has properly investigated the case and submitted the charge- sheet that there are no false implication of vehicle or accused by the Investigating Officer.
On all these grounds sought for dismissal of appeal.
6. A perusal of the material placed before the Tribunal, it is crystal clear that the complaint filed by the complainant/Abdul Samad.

Bidar Traffic police have registered case in Crime No.62/2016 against the unknown accused/driver of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/S-4534 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC r/w 187 of IMV Act and submitted FIR to the Court.
Thereafter police have rushed to the spot and conducted the spot panchanama.
At the time of panchanama police have taken the possession of Hero Honda bearing Reg.No.KA-38/H-6366 which was involved in this accident.
The Motor Vehicle Inspector, investigated the vehicle on 13.05.2016 near traffic police station premises.
The Investigating Officer has also recorded further statement on 14.05.2016 as per Ex.P7.

The Investigating Officer obtained wound certificate and recorded the statement of witnesses and submitted charge-sheet/P.4 against the rider of the offending vehicle for offences punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Section 187 of MV Act.

7. The Tribunal has observed in para-14 of its judgment that the counsel for respondent No.2 has cross examined the petitioner in length, but during the course of cross-examination nothing is revealed so as to disbelieve the evidences of PW.1 so far as accident is concerned and injury sustained by him.

Upon considering the oral evidence of PW.1 and analyzing the evidence with reference to the cross- examination, this Court is of the opinion that, it is proved that PW.1 is telling truth before the court regarding injury sustained.

The evidence of PW.1 corroborated with the documentary evidence as per Ex.P1 to 97.
8.
On re-appreciation of evidence on record, I do not find any legal infirmities in the finding given by the Tribunal.

Apart from this, during the course of cross-examination of RW.1 he has clearly admitted that he has not lodged any complaint against the Investigating Officer that he has recorded false statement on 11.05.2016.
He has also not challenged the charge-sheet before the Court of law or before the higher authority.
Further he has submitted that he has made personal enquiry regarding this accident, but he has not submitted the report.
Further he has stated that it is internal report.
Even if it is internal report, if it is in favour of insurance company he could have produce the same before the Tribunal to rebut the evidence of claimant, but he has not done so.
Viewed from any angle, that there is no legal evidence to discard evidence placed by the claimant.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
(ii) The amount deposited before this Court, if  any, by the insurance company is directed  to be transmitted to the concerned  Tribunal.
